claim: Carbohydrate foods commonly have the most direct effect on blood glucose.
The diabetes plate pattern uses non-starchy vegetables, protein, carbohydrate, and a low-calorie drink.
supporting_source: ADA Diabetes Food Hub, What is the Diabetes Plate?

claim: Percent Daily Value can help identify whether a nutrient is high or low; 5% low and 20% high.
FDA Daily Value for dietary fiber is 28 g based on 2,000 calories.
Daily Value for added sugars is 50 g based on 2,000 calories; Dietary Guidelines recommend less than 10% calories from added sugars.
Lifestyle changes can help prevent or delay type 2 diabetes for people at high risk, but are not guarantees.
Both high and low blood sugar can affect the brain and require individualized targets.
AHA recommends emphasizing unsaturated fats in place of saturated and trans fats.
